runs.text: Define one finite set of structured objects, then partition or enumerate that same set in two different ways.
Equating the two totals yields an identity without requiring an explicit bijection between two separately defined sets.
The first counts vertex-edge incidences in a finite undirected graph. The second counts a k-subset with one selected member, either choosing the subset first or the marked member first.

items.text: Both computations must count exactly the same structured objects, including multiplicity.
In a simple undirected graph every edge contributes two incidences; loops require an explicit degree convention.
Marking an object changes the counted set and must be included on both sides.
For infinite sets, cardinal sums need extra justification; the handbook formulas here are finite.
